q: How do I stop the same invoice being counted twice in my carbon report?
title: Stop one invoice being counted twice
short: Use two checks. A file fingerprint (SHA-256 hash) blocks the exact same file being uploaded again. A business key, the supplier's GSTIN plus invoice number and date, catches the same invoice arriving as a new scan, photo or email copy, which a file hash cannot. Review any match before deleting it.

sections.h: What a file hash catches and what it misses
p: SHA-256 turns a file's bytes into a fixed 64-character fingerprint. The same file always gives the same fingerprint, so re-uploading it is caught. Change one byte, such as a new scan of the same paper bill or the same PDF saved again, and the fingerprint is completely different. A hash proves a file is identical; it cannot tell that two different files show the same invoice.

ol: Build a key from supplier GSTIN, invoice number and invoice date.
For e-invoices, use the Invoice Reference Number (IRN), which is unique per e-invoice.
For electricity bills, compare the site, billing period and units billed.
Flag any second document with the same key and hold it out of the totals until someone reviews it.

sections.h: Where double counting usually comes from
ul: The same bill uploaded by two people in one company.
A proforma invoice and the final tax invoice for one purchase.
A delivery challan and the invoice for the same diesel.
Monthly statements that repeat invoices already uploaded.
Electricity bills with arrears that rebill units from a previous period.
Credit notes and revised invoices: the revision should replace, not add to, the original.

sections.h: Why it matters for your report
p: The GHG Protocol accuracy principle asks that emissions are neither overstated nor understated. A duplicate overstates your footprint, distorts your base year and can mislead a buyer or lender. Auditors test for it by sorting the listing on supplier and invoice number, so check this yourself before they do.

example.title: Worked example: a diesel invoice counted twice
lines: Invoice: 1,000 litres of diesel x 2.68 = 2,680 kg CO2
A photo of the same invoice and the emailed PDF both uploaded: 5,360 kg CO2 reported
Different files, so different SHA-256 fingerprints: the hash check does not catch it
Same GSTIN, invoice number and date: the business key check flags it, and 2,680 kg is removed

senseible: Senseible fingerprints every file with SHA-256 and counts an identical file once, including when different members of one organisation upload it. That check matches byte-identical files only, so a re-scan or a photo of the same bill needs the invoice number and GSTIN check described here.

sources.label: NIST FIPS PUB 180-4, Secure Hash Standard
